rounds.method_summary: Selects highly uncertain comparisons while enforcing diversity in a randomized low-dimensional projection of the pair features via farthest-point sampling. This combines informative near-ties with broad coverage rather than spending the budget on redundant uncertainty-only pairs, addressing the absence of prior feedback with a robust exploration/exploitation design.

rounds.method_summary: Select one pair per prompt using logistic Fisher trace, combining uncertainty with feature-difference magnitude while reserving a small decaying fraction for random and high-norm exploration. I chose this prompt-balanced, fully vectorized rule in response to the timeout feedback, eliminating projection construction and repeated greedy scans. Implementation note: candidate rows are shuffled upstream; the 45-row blocks used here are arbitrary candidate blocks and do not guarantee one pair per prompt.

Use prompt-balanced logistic Fisher acquisition with a diagonal-whitened feature norm, so hidden dimensions contribute by standardized leverage rather than raw activation scale. Based on the retained Fisher result and timeout feedback, this removes randomized exploration and uses only inexpensive vectorized reductions while introducing a new covariance-aware information criterion. Implementation note: candidate rows are shuffled upstream; the 45-row blocks used here are arbitrary candidate blocks and do not guarantee one pair per prompt.

Replace diagonal whitening with a ridge-regularized full-covariance Mahalanobis leverage score, then select the highest logistic Fisher-information pair independently for every prompt. This retains the successful prompt-balanced Fisher strategy while using one small eigendecomposition and vectorized matrix operations, avoiding the timed-out projection and greedy scans. Implementation note: candidate rows are shuffled upstream; the 45-row blocks used here are arbitrary candidate blocks and do not guarantee one pair per prompt.

Use a fully vectorized prompt-balanced score combining stable logistic uncertainty with a capped raw feature norm, replacing the expensive covariance eigendecomposition and projections. The score also adapts mildly by round so later acquisition values feature-space informativeness without any greedy scans or repeated distance calculations, directly addressing the timeout feedback. Implementation note: candidate rows are shuffled upstream; the 45-row blocks used here are arbitrary candidate blocks and do not guarantee one pair per prompt.

Use prompt-balanced Fisher acquisition with leverage measured in a candidate-weighted logistic Fisher geometry rather than the unweighted covariance of the current best. This is a new uncertainty-aware information-matrix criterion implemented with one 64-dimensional Cholesky solve and vectorized scoring, avoiding the projection-plus-greedy approach implicated in the timeout feedback. Implementation note: candidate rows are shuffled upstream; the 45-row blocks used here are arbitrary candidate blocks and do not guarantee one pair per prompt.

Approximate the retained full-covariance Fisher-leverage strategy with an eight-dimensional randomized covariance range, while modeling omitted directions using their residual energy and average variance. This preserves prompt-balanced uncertainty and anisotropy scoring but replaces the expensive 64-dimensional covariance projection with substantially smaller vectorized matrix products in response to the timeout feedback. Implementation note: candidate rows are shuffled upstream; the 45-row blocks used here are arbitrary candidate blocks and do not guarantee one pair per prompt.
